nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable supply chains|Supply chain collaboration_qna_000
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the significance of comparing the profit models of the three-layer integrated supply chain and the individual profit models?
nodes.answer: Comparing the profit models helps in determining the most viable model for the supply chain operations.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable supply chains|Supply chain collaboration_qna_001
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What is lead time aggregation in a three-echelon supply chain model?
nodes.answer: Lead time aggregation in a three-echelon supply chain model refers to the process of combining lead times at different levels of the supply chain to make more accurate and efficient decisions regarding inventory management and distribution.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable supply chains|Supply chain collaboration_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why do some supply chain actors show low motivation towards information exchange?
nodes.answer: The fear of information loss due to shared information is a significant factor that hinders motivation for information exchange among supply chain actors, as highlighted by Carter and Rogers (2008).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable supply chains|Supply chain collaboration_qna_003
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How do companies view cooperation among FSC actors in pursuing sustainable goals?
nodes.answer: Companies agree that cooperation among FSC actors benefits sustainable goals, as reflected in relationship performances being closer to the "often" option for all actions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable supply chains|Supply chain collaboration_qna_004
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How can collaboration among fashion industry players help improve competitiveness, image, and reputation while reducing costs?
nodes.answer: Collaboration between players within the fashion industry can increase competitiveness with an improved image and reputation and reduced costs, as highlighted by Rest et al. (2018).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable supply chains|Supply chain collaboration_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do uniform and co-existing asymmetries in supply chain relationships impact product development?
nodes.answer: Uniform asymmetry restricts technical capability development and sustainability orientation, while co-existing asymmetry hinders collaboration, knowledge sharing, and critical path management, thereby affecting supply chain relations and SPD negatively.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable supply chains|Supply chain collaboration_qna_006
nodes.question: What collaborative effort is being made to improve the sustainability of global supply chains?
nodes.answer: A new ambitious multi-country collaboration is linking international trade systems to social and environmental impacts to address the sustainability of natural resource supply chains and help mitigate biodiversity loss on a large scale.
